description: Standard mixed-task inventory: RoBERTa-base LoRA adapters across distinct classification tasks (hate speech, news, sentiment, MNLI). Tests whether Gradience narrows mixed-task space sensibly.
trial_purpose: Test the core use case. See whether Gradience identifies meaningful task boundaries and narrows candidate pairs to a plausible evaluation subset.

adapters.notes: Binary hate speech detection on tweets.
4-class news topic classification (World, Sports, Business, Sci/Tech).
Binary irony detection on tweets. Source model had prior sentiment training.
MNLI 3-class NLI. Different label space from the binary classifiers. Older format (adapter_model.bin not safetensors).
AG News adapter from a formality-pretrained source. Same task as the other AG News adapter but different training lineage.

selection_rationale: Five adapters, four distinct tasks, all on roberta-base. Two share a task (ag_news) with different training lineage — tests same-task detection. Hate speech and irony are both tweet-domain binary classifiers — tests whether Gradience sees them as related or distinct. MNLI is structurally different (3-class NLI). This inventory should produce meaningful task-boundary signals and a non-trivial candidate space reduction.

expected_gradience_behavior.same_task_safe_zones: Two AG News adapters should be same-task safe
expected_gradience_behavior.cross_task_caution: MNLI adapter is structurally different — should trigger cross-task advisory. Hate/irony pair may show task-boundary signal.
expected_gradience_behavior.exclusions: Possibly the MNLI adapter if label-space mismatch is detected
expected_gradience_behavior.overall: Mixed posture, moderate reduction, 2-3 retained pairs
